note: Every gate verify.sh reports as NOT COVERED on a CI runner, and why. The 'Every gate ran and every gap is named' step in verify.yml fails on any gap or skipped test not listed here for that runner, so a gate that starts skipping for a new reason cannot pass as green. A skip listed here that stops happening is reported, not failed. An entry may carry `modes` (default, race, fuzz) to hold only for that verify.sh invocation; without it the entry holds in all three. Every entry names the `legs` it belongs to (go-test, rust, checks, bench: the verify.sh legs CI runs as separate jobs): a log is compared only against the entries of its own leg, so an entry for one leg cannot excuse the same text from another, and an entry that names no leg excuses nothing in a leg run. `fuzz_floors` holds the --fuzz targets that do not reach MANVI_FUZZMIN inputs inside MANVI_FUZZMAX: verify.sh names each such target with its count, and CI accepts the line only while the count is at or above the target's floor, so a slow target that gets slower still fails and an unlisted one fails at once. Each floor is a quarter of the lowest count in three CI runs (44540872844, 44571487515, 44589548386; ubuntu-latest, 120s cap). The same target varied up to 4.2x between those runs, so a tighter floor would fail on runner noise.

gaps.text: bench/stress_test.py: C6 fork denial — the bwrap profile has no seccomp filter, so a Linux worker can fork (the macOS sandbox-exec profile denies it)
gaps.why: Denying fork under bwrap needs a seccomp filter the bench does not build. The Linux worker's helpers stay inside its pid and network namespaces and die with it, and C6 shows they cannot read the hidden tests or signal the harness.
